      "observations": [
        "Owned two-file human patch read in full. The production hunk restores MimeParser.getParameter(fullContentType, \"name\") when Content-Disposition filename is empty, replacing structured contentType.get(\"name\"). The patch preserves the empty-string fallback. Current accepted WebExtMimeTreeEmitter still gives Content-Disposition filename priority, then the full Content-Type name, with separate forwarded-message and deleted-placeholder fallbacks. Existing focused lesson 5bdcff… already captures that contract; reuse it rather than duplicate its whole analysis.",
        "The current comm MimeParser wrapper unfolds continued header whitespace, looks up parameter names case-insensitively, and passes true for both RFC2047 encoded-word and RFC2231 parameter decoding flags. The owned fixture is application/octet-stream with attachment disposition but no disposition filename, and a split RFC2047-encoded Content-Type name. The new direct assertion expects Rechnung 2025-1056119.pdf. This is a deliberate encoded-name fixture, not a malformed test to rewrite or a complete parser correctness proof.",
        "The added task directly checks one listed message, one returned attachment, partName 1.1 and its decoded name. It calls listAttachments, despite the bug report concerning getAttachmentFile. Current listAttachments converts MimeTreePart.name into MessageAttachment.name; getAttachmentFile uses MsgHdrProcessor.getAttachmentPart and passes the resulting attachmentPart.name to the File constructor. Both parser entry points use the custom attachment emitter. The source therefore connects the fix to both APIs, while only the list name is directly asserted by this new task. No claim of independent File.name or saved-file coverage follows from that test.",
        "Both setup and task explicitly skip IMAP. The task uses test3, accountsRead/messagesRead permissions, startup, awaitFinish and unload. Its four browser.test.assertEq calls omit third-argument messages, including the multiline decoded-name comparison. Add nonempty expected-behavior messages when editing them; a task name or Request attachments comment is not a message. The existing task name mentions text-as-attachment while the new fixture is an encoded filename on application/octet-stream; a descriptive encoded-name task name would make this scoped regression easier to find, without imposing a global naming rule.",
        "Exact retained primary Bug1992976 current description/comments0–4 and footer were read. The reporter supplies the encoded header/name and intended decoded value while withholding the private user message. A commenter attributes the regression to the structured header accessor; author acknowledges it and links the patch. No private message, linked issue or prior patch was fetched. Full own D271298 was already read during the collector and has no submitted inlines or summary/test-plan edits. Approval/build/landing entries remain historical context."

      "observations": [
        "Owned human patch read in full across registration, schema and 19 new test-case lines. It adds readerDisplayAttachmentsInline as a messengerSettings-permission protected types.Setting property backed by mail.inline_attachments. The registration has only getCallback, and the API explicitly passes readOnly:true to getSettingsAPI. The schema now explicitly documents read-only status for the two older outgoing-message settings as well; this does not make all messengerSettings properties read-only. Accepted composeInlineSpellCheckEnabled is a separate writable setting with setCallback.",
        "The comm MIME setup reads mail.inline_attachments into show_attachment_inline_p, with distinct text-inline and reply-quote flags. The setting returns a global preference rather than measuring an individual rendered attachment. Accepted default is true, while mail.inline_attachments.text defaults false. Selected MIME gating also considers forceInline and quoting state. The schema says supported attachment types; no third-party Audio Preview behavior or every-media rendering guarantee follows from this preference alone.",
        "The two added test cases expect value:true/not_controllable, then use a privileged parent message handler to set mail.inline_attachments false and expect value:false/not_controllable. The shared window.assertDeepEqual receives expected, awaited .get({}) result, a nonempty message naming the test index/setting and containing should, and strict:true. This directly checks returned value/control metadata, without attempting an extension .set/.clear on the read-only property or asserting onChange delivery. The engine ExtensionPreferencesManager implementation is an unpaired bounded dependency, not public evidence here.",
        "Test cleanup finding: clearUserPrefs omits mail.inline_attachments both in the historical test and accepted test. The new false case uses Services.prefs.setBoolPref through the parent handler, but the helper registered for setup/end only clears older settings (and later spellcheck). A scoped repair should add the newly changed preference to that helper so its own setup/cleanup matches its Start with defaults/Return to defaults comments. This is a local source omission, not an observed failure in a later task or a claim that separate xpcshell processes share preference state.",
        "Naming follows the existing camelCase Setting names and private pref spelling; the public name/read-only option and schema description agree. The indexed test loop uses idx to identify a scenario in failure output, so an index serves a real diagnostic role. Comments explain default restoration and the later AddonManager dependency rather than defining a universal test pattern. Complete retained Bug1988561 description/comments0–2/footer was read: initial API placement options become the explicit read-only messengerSettings choice. Own full D271357 has no submitted inlines/summary/test-plan edits; historical landing does not add execution proof."
